safeguards: gltf::Gltf::from_slice invokes its document validation before the fixture continues; neither optional reader values nor a malformed source assumption alone prove a particular GLB is accepted.

The fixture explicitly rejects a missing binary blob and missing node with both skin and mesh. The skin and mesh unwraps after that exact predicate are guarded; the later primitive and morph-position unwraps require independent proof.

RuntimeBody::validate rejects empty vertices/faces, inconsistent array lengths and mismatched joint counts. GpuBody::new additionally checks selected face indices before upload. These guards do not themselves check chart finiteness or a nonzero body height.

candidates.classification: New bounded current fixture admission and rule trace, related to earlier GLB input questions without altering historical unique count.
candidates.trace: The shared armor_fixture::load function is compiled into the browser probe example and returns Result, but uses unwrap on the selected mesh primitive and on each morph position iterator. Pinned crates/AGENTS.md forbids unwrap or expect outside tests. The prior search for a node containing both a skin and mesh protects the following two node access unwraps under stable source semantics; no panic is claimed for those guarded calls. The pinned gltf 1.4.1 parser validates documents, while its morph reader exposes optional POSITION, NORMAL and TANGENT iterators. If a parsed body reaches a morph target whose position iterator is None, the direct p.unwrap would panic rather than return the function error; a primitive-free selected mesh has an analogous conditional unwrap. No GLB byte sequence was constructed, parsed or executed, and accepted input, external support policy and browser panic presentation remain unproven.
candidates.connected_repair: At the fixture boundary, destructure already checked node values and propagate contextual errors for a missing primitive or unsupported/missing morph data, or deliberately support a valid no-position morph by using unchanged positions after confirming the input contract. Preserve canonical GLB geometry, morph correspondence and native/browser Result behavior. Do not weaken parser validation or add compatibility shims.
candidates.discovery: partial; exact accepted GLB witnesses, canonical-body input policy, all example callers and parser/version behavior remain open

candidates.severity: unassigned; conditional nonfinite fixture surface-coordinate admission
candidates.classification: New bounded source-derived arithmetic and aggregate-admission question; distinct producer and value from the earlier offline GLB body-normal export finding.
candidates.trace: The fixture builds a cylindrical surface chart using (y - low) / (high - low) and then embeds those coordinates in RuntimeBody. For any nonempty finite position set with a single y value, the numerator and denominator are both zero, giving a NaN v coordinate. A hypothetical nondegenerate triangle with positions (0,0,0), (1,0,0), (0,0,1) has this property. If a parsed skinned body reaches this chart with otherwise matching valid normals, indices, joints and weights, the selected RuntimeBody::validate checks lengths, joint counts and nonempty faces but does not check coordinate finiteness or vertical extent. The selected GpuBody::new similarly checks lengths and face indices before passing the texcoords to its upload boundary; no GPU execution, accepted GLB, successful upload or invalid rendered mesh is claimed. The canonical humanoid may satisfy the intended nonzero-height precondition; no evidence establishes that the shipped body triggers this.
candidates.connected_repair: Establish the supported body geometry admission at the earliest boundary and reject zero/invalid height or deliberately define a valid chart for it. Carry a finite, topology-consistent chart through RuntimeBody and the device boundary, preserving the ordinary nondegenerate canonical body and explicit error context. Coordinate with the separately recorded offline normal export and clothing-face findings without merging different first failures.
